newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans flock to invest abroad in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Germans flock to invest abroad in 1997.

text.p: German investors poured billions of marks into foreign share markets in the first few months of 1997, nearly matching the total for all of 1996, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday in its monthly report for June.
The German central bank said 55 billion marks ($31.8 billion) flowed out of Germany during the four month period from January to April, almost equal to last year's total of 60.5 billion marks.
"It is interesting to note the clearly rising interest of domestic investors in foreign share markets," the report said.
The report said surging global share markets, along with a lack of attractive fixed-interest offerings in Germany due to low interest rates, led to the high interest in foreign offerings.
The Bundesbank also said foreign investment in the German share market during the four-month period rose to 43.5 billion marks from 38 billion marks in the last four months of 1996.
But investments dropped off in March and April during a bout of profit-taking by foreign investors.
In debt markets, the Bundesbank said net sales in foreign and domestic bonds rose to 147.3 billion marks from 83.2 billion in the previous four months.
Foreign bonds with a value of 20.0 billion marks were sold over the period, a sharp rise from the 5.0 billion mark level during the last third of 1996.

"This rise was due to greater interest for foreign-currency denominated bonds among domestic investors, who invested 19.6 billion marks in such paper over the period compared with 3.1 billion marks previously," the report said.
The Bundebsank added that foreign investors were notably interested in two-year debt contracts.
